content: Don't bend; don't water it down; don't try to make it logical; don't edit your own soul according to the fashion. Rather, follow your most intense obsessions mercilessly.
author: Franz Kafka
story:
Working exhausting days as an insurance bureaucrat in Prague under the shadow of a domineering father, Kafka wrote late into the night while dying of tuberculosis. In nightmarish, haunting fables, he chronicled the alienation, bureaucratic labyrinth, and existential guilt of modern life, creating art of breathtaking sensitivity and modern resonance.

This timeless reminder speaks to the universal struggle to balance inner truth with outer demands. Franz Kafka understood that the measure of a meaningful life is not external approval, but the quiet integrity with which we meet each day's encounters.
reflectionPrompt: How can you welcome mistakes and awkward beginnings as essential steps in your creative evolution?
